summary: Contains the text of a statement signed on 29 August 2012 by the IEEE Standards Association, the IAB, the IETF, the Internet Society and the W3C. It affirms a set of principles, known as OpenStand, for open, jointly developed global standards. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC publishes a statement signed by leaders of five standards organizations. It describes principles they affirm for developing and adopting global standards.

questions: what are the modern paradigm for standards principles
what does rfc 6852 say about voluntary adoption
subtitle: A signed affirmation of principles for open, global standards development.

tldr.problem: The leaders of five standards organizations wanted to affirm shared principles for a modern global standards paradigm.
tldr.mechanism: They signed a statement supporting cooperation, due process, broad consensus, transparency, balance, openness, availability, and voluntary adoption.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6852 publishes the text of the affirmation as an informational record.

today: RFC 6852 is an Informational record of the OpenStand affirmation signed by the listed organizations on 29 August 2012.

sections.title: The OpenStand Affirmation
sections.content:
On 29 August 2012, leaders of the IEEE Standards Association, IAB, IETF, Internet Society, and W3C signed a statement about principles for global, open standards. The memo says these became known as the OpenStand principles.

RFC 6852 records the signed statement and invites others to support its principles. It is not an Internet Standards Track specification.
sections.plainLanguage: Leaders from five organizations signed a shared statement about standards. This RFC preserves the statement as a record.

sections.title: Principles for Standards Work
sections.content:
The statement describes cooperation among standards organizations and adherence to standards-development principles: due process, broad consensus, transparency, balance, and openness. It also calls for collective empowerment and standards based on technical merit.

It says specifications should be available for implementation under fair terms, which may range from royalty-free to fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory terms. Standards are voluntarily adopted, and success is determined by the market.
sections.plainLanguage: The statement calls for fair, open processes that consider different views. It also says standards should be available to implement and adopted voluntarily.

sections.title: The Signed Statement and Invitation
sections.content:
The affirmation says open, participatory standards support interoperability and global competition and can serve as building blocks for products and services. It connects voluntary adoption with innovation and market growth.

The signatories state their support for and adherence to the principles. The document invites other standards organizations, governments, corporations, and technology innovators to support them as well.
sections.plainLanguage: The signatories commit to the statement's principles and invite others to do the same. The RFC records that invitation and their affirmation.
